hook: On a disk, clumping cells generically blow up once mass reaches 4 pi, and never below it.
summary: The Keller-Segel model describes cells that attract each other through a chemical signal. The authors prove that on a disk, mass of at least 4 pi sends an open dense set of starting densities to blow-up or unbounded growth over infinite time, while lower mass always settles to a smooth equilibrium. They extend sharp thresholds to other planar domains, the sphere and the square torus. It is a mathematical result for one idealized model.
title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
